## Asunción, the capital of Paraguay

Asunción stands on the Paraná River and is regarded as the world's least expensive capital. On Avenida Colón, one of the city's oldest streets, you will find the famous Recova, an entire district of souvenir stalls where you can buy lace that is renowned around the world.

## Asunción: Paraguay's tourist centre

The most prestigious residential neighbourhoods lie east of the city centre, in Recoleta and Villa Morra. Many embassies, restaurants and nightclubs are also found here. The city has several beautiful parks, including Jardín Botánico. Within its grounds are a golf course, a zoo, the house of Don Carlos Antonio López, which has been converted into a natural history museum and library, and a museum of Indigenous culture. Be sure to try the national drink, Paraguayan tea known as mate, prepared from the leaves of young shoots of a holly-family plant.

Across the Atacama Salt Flat, the landscape shifts from rough salt crust to shallow pools of water. One of the stops is Chaxa Lagoon, where flamingos can be observed.

A visit to the salt flat is combined with Socaire, Toconao and the high-altitude lagoons. Together, these places reveal different aspects of the Atacama: dry plateaus, volcanic slopes, small settlements and salt plains.

Atins is a small coastal village in Maranhão state, on the edge of the dunes of Lençóis Maranhenses. Sandy streets, low houses and palm trees create a tranquil atmosphere, while the surrounding area combines the seashore with broad expanses of pale sand.

Atins is one of the stops on journeys through Lençóis Maranhenses. Excursions in the surrounding area focus on the dunes and seasonal lagoons, while time in the village itself is devoted to the coast and unhurried walks. The natural landscape changes through the year with the rains and water levels.
